The criterion (section 5) written in notes-C5.md before pass 1: prefer a later account when it states fewer unmarked causal sentences, tells at least as many of the 35 pass 5 story rooms (16 told, 19 with a residue) without a residue with no more elements, keeps every tested arrow, passes more names on the prose test, and at the check legs lets the readers recover more of what I meant; reject one that gains reach by loosening an element or by an unsupported sentence. The declaration prose rule written before reading any declaration: in prose, changed and mistaken_for, a universal, comparative, causal or cyclic sentence about the rooms stands only on an order count that beats its null, a finding, a count in structure-C4.md or a setting fact the contract states; otherwise it is rewritten to say what members did in how many rooms, each act shown by a member's quote; names, members and the cut change only if the quotes show the theme joins what its construct keeps apart; each amendment a tier_history line, a move logged and snapped. Next: read Heylighen 2016 and Grasse 1959 whole.

Read Heylighen (2016) whole from out/sources-from-J/heylighen-2016.md (pages 4 to 13). Claims taken, verified: stigmergy defined as 'an indirect, mediated mechanism of coordination between actions, in which the trace of an action left on a medium stimulates the performance of a subsequent action' (p. 6; abstract p. 4); coordinated activity 'without any need for planning, control, communication, simultaneous presence, or even mutual awareness' (p. 4); the trace makes an action more probable, neither necessary nor sufficient (p. 7); a trace may be unplanned, while 'markers' are intentional signs, and some stigmergy relies on them (p. 8); letting 'the agents communicate about their work' is the alternative to stigmergy, while a website registering the state of the work is 'a medium providing special markers' (p. 9); 'no need for the agents to negotiate about who does what' (p. 10); repair of a broken column is negative feedback on the trace (p. 11). Next: Grasse (1959), in pages.

Read Grasse (1959) whole from out/sources-from-J/grasse-1959.md (pages 41 to 80, French OCR; translations mine). Claims taken, verified: 'La coordination des taches, la regulation des constructions ne dependent pas directement des ouvriers, mais des constructions elles-memes. L'ouvrier ne dirige pas son travail, il est guide par lui' (p. 65), the definition of stigmergy; the masons do not build in teams (p. 65; summary p. 79, 'Masons do not constitute a working team'); the only important guide is the material work done (p. 71); stigmergy is set apart from reciprocal stimulation between individuals, as in nuptial parades (pp. 74-75); no need to appeal to relations between individuals or to a plan (p. 75), though cooperation or information between workers is not ruled out, and nothing like the bees' dance was seen (p. 75); repair and new building use the same technique (p. 58); 'Stigmergy clearly explains the correlation between the tasks achieved and does not require any further explanation involving a given plan' (summary, p. 79). Both sources keep coordination through the work apart from communication between members; Heylighen (p. 9) admits a shared record of the work's state as a medium of markers.

Abductive read, prompted by Grasse (1959) and Heylighen (2016), logged before it runs; rules written first in notes-C5.md. Question: does Stigmergy as cut join what its sources keep apart, coordination through the work and communication between members? Sample: T3-038 and T3-041, 24 records each, seed 20261015, at most two per room; T3-060 every record up to 24 (c5_stigmergy_sample.py). Codes: M (the trace or a marker: the work's state reported, or an act on what the canvas showed), MP (a proposal grounded in a named state of the canvas, counted with M), P (a proposal or request to others with no state of the canvas named), O (other). Rule: a member joins what the sources keep apart if P is at least half of its records not O; T3-041 would then move to Collective representation; T3-038 would be reported, not split, in this pass.

Abductive read of Stigmergy, result (c5_stigmergy_codes.json, c5_stigmergy_tally.py): T3-038 M 9, MP 1, P 5, O 9 (P 5 of 15 not O); T3-041 M 5, MP 4, P 8, O 7 (P 8 of 17, 0.47); T3-060 M 11, MP 1, P 8, O 4 (P 8 of 20). No member meets the rule written first (P at least half of records not O), so Stigmergy keeps its cut; no recut. T3-041 is close: one doubtful code (warriors/c0119, coded MP) recoded as P would move it to 9 of 17. Across the three members, 31 of 52 records not O report the work's state or act on what the canvas showed (markers in Heylighen's sense, p. 9), and 21 of 52 are proposals or requests to others with no state of the canvas named. The declaration must say both. Coded by me alone. Next: Stigmergy's declaration amended under the prose rule, with the sources verified.
